answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity lock a slashable bond and build a checkable history, like basalt anchoring a trellis while a steady pulse of attestations proves real work over time. Peers only credit identities with bonded history, so fresh fakes earn nothing. An attacker must fund a separate bond and do real work for every fake, and loses the bond if caught, so mass identities cost real capital instead of being free.
